faq.a: Most atoms are about 0.1 to 0.3 nanometres across. A nanometre is a millionth of a millimetre, so a few million atoms in a row would fit across a full stop.
An atom has a tiny nucleus in the middle, made of protons and neutrons, with electrons moving around it. Most of the atom is empty space.
asks: What is an atom made of?

faq.a: The nucleus is tens of thousands of times smaller than the whole atom, yet it holds almost all of the atom's mass.
Not with an ordinary light microscope, because atoms are far smaller than the waves of light. Special microscopes, like the scanning tunnelling microscope, can map single atoms.
asks: Can we see atoms with a microscope?

faq.q: How many particles are in a grain of salt?
faq.a: A small grain of salt holds roughly a billion billion particles of sodium and chloride. That is a 1 followed by 18 zeros.
asks: How many atoms are in a grain of salt?

facts: Atoms are typically about 0.1 to 0.3 nanometres across.
The nucleus contains nearly all of an atom's mass but is tens of thousands of times smaller than the atom.

quiz.say: Which list goes from biggest to smallest?
quiz.show: Which list goes from biggest to smallest?
quiz.why: A grain holds billions of atoms, and the nucleus is a tiny part of one atom.

wrong.0: A salt grain is made of billions of atoms, so it is bigger than an atom.
wrong.1: That list goes from smallest to biggest.

quiz.say: What fills most of the space inside an atom?
quiz.show: What fills most of the space inside an atom?
quiz.why: The nucleus is tiny; electrons move around it in mostly empty space.

wrong.0: Neutrons are also packed into the tiny nucleus.
wrong.2: Protons sit in the tiny nucleus.
